result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the fear of being wrong.

Not just in science or art, but in every conversation, every policy, every relationship. Imagine a world where people could say, *"I don’t know"* without shame, where mistakes weren’t met with ridicule but curiosity, where progress wasn’t stifled by the need to be right.

It would mean fewer wars fought over ideology, fewer careers ruined by a single misstep, fewer children growing up believing their worth is tied to perfection. It would mean more collaboration, more innovation, more humanity.

Because the truth is, we’re all wrong about something. The difference between a broken world and a thriving one might just be how we handle that.
